extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media professionals, business leaders, policymakers and the general public interested in public-trust metrics
extracted.subtask_description: A corporate press release/report summarizing the 2018 Edelman Trust Barometer survey results — global and country trust indices across institutions and demographics, with highlighted changes and explanatory analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Trust Index
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Index is an average of a country’s trust in the institutions of government, business, media and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the headline metric for country-level comparisons (e.g., 'Global 64'). Values are based on percent trust / average percent trust. The index aggregates across the four institutional dimensions to produce an overall country score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional trust dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust is measured separately for the institutions of government, business, media and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report compares levels and changes in trust across these four institutions (e.g., 'People’s trust in business, government, NGOs and media remained largely unchanged from 2017'). Analysts should report each institution’s score as well as aggregates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust category thresholds
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these bands to classify country or population groups by their overall trust level. The thresholds define interpretive categories for reporting and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience segments: Informed Public
rubrics_metrics.description: All informed public respondents met the following criteria: aged 25-64, college-educated; household income in the top quartile for their age in their country; read or watch business/news media at least several times a week; follow public policy issues in the news at least several times a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Informed Public' is a defined survey segment; analyses and claims about this audience must use these inclusion criteria when comparing to the mass population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience segments: Mass population
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass population respondents are aged 18+ and represent the portion of the population that do not meet the criteria for the Informed Public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish findings for the mass population from the informed public; the two groups are measured and reported separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-level trust change / polarization
rubrics_metrics.description: The world is moving apart in trust; for the first time there is a distinct split between extreme trust gainers and losers (e.g., 'No country saw steeper declines than the United States, with a 37-point aggregate drop... China experienced a 27-point gain').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report year-on-year aggregate point changes across institutions for countries to identify gainers and losers; highlight large swings and polarization trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media composition and source-type breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust Barometer respondents hold a broad definition of 'media' that includes platforms such as social media (48 percent) and search engines (25 percent), alongside journalism (89 percent) which includes publishers and news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting media trust, separate 'platforms', 'journalism', and 'peer' sources because different components show divergent credibility trends and can drive aggregate media trust results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists have risen in credibility (examples: 'journalism jumped five points' and elsewhere 'Journalists have risen 12 points' depending on context/population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track point changes in perceived credibility for journalists across years and audiences; note paradoxes where journalism credibility rises even as 'media' as an institution falls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in platforms dipped (example: 'trust in platforms dipped two points').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure platforms (social media, search engines) separately from journalism and report changes, as platform declines may drive overall media distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of 'a person like yourself' (peer sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: The credibility of 'a person like yourself' — often a source of news and information on social media — dipped to an all-time low in the study’s history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include peer-source credibility as a distinct metric; declines here are relevant to understanding trust in social channels and the spread of misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concern about fake news / ability to identify reputable news
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly seven in 10 respondents among the general population worry about fake news or false information being used as a weapon, and 59 percent say that it is getting harder to tell if a piece of news was produced by a respected media organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both the percentage expressing worry about fake news and the percentage who find it harder to identify respected news sources; these are indicators of the information environment and drivers of media distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of experts and business leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Voices of expertise are regaining credibility: 'Journalists have risen 12 points, and CEOs recorded a seven-percentage point gain... Technical experts, financial industry analysts, and successful entrepreneurs now register credibility levels of 50 percent or higher.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report credibility levels and point changes for various expert categories (CEOs, technical experts, analysts, entrepreneurs); note threshold interpretations (e.g., ≥50% as a meaningful credibility level).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic breakdowns for trust analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore trust by institution, gender, age, and audience (the site invites users to 'Select a country on the left to explore trust by institution, gender, age, and audience').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate trust measures by demographic dimensions (gender, age cohorts, and audience segments) when presenting results to reveal subgroup differences and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement notes: values and averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Values based on percent trust; Values based on average percent trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about whether reported figures are raw percent-trust responses or averages across items when presenting scores; this affects comparability and interpretation.
